findings.finding: Backend/frontend contract mismatch renders the new moderator evidence non-functional as merged.
findings.evidence: Backend (rentals/backend/src/routes/admin.ts:517-531, spreading `...r` from Prisma) returns `qualifyingInteraction` as a bare enum scalar string, e.g. "SHARED_CONVERSATION". Frontend (rentals/frontend/src/app/admin/page.tsx:389-398) expects an object shape: `r.qualifyingInteraction.type` and `r.qualifyingInteraction.listing?.title`. Since a string has no `.type`/`.listing` properties, every ternary branch evaluates to undefined/false, so the admin panel will render an empty 'Qualifying interaction: ' line with no actual evidence for every USER report going forward, and the listing title is never shown for the two listing-based paths at all (backend never joins/returns a listing for this field). This is not an exploitable vulnerability (no auth bypass, no injection, no unintended data exposure -- React safely renders undefined as nothing), but it means the shipped feature fails to deliver the moderator-visible evidence that was the entire point of this task and that Trust & Safety specifically requested to help judge report legitimacy.
findings.recommendedAction: Reconcile the contract before merge: either have admin.ts map the scalar into { type, listing } (joining the relevant listing when the path is LISTING_MESSAGED/LISTING_SAVED) to match what the frontend already expects, or simplify the frontend to render the plain scalar string directly. Re-verify by hitting GET /admin/reports against a real USER report of each of the three types and confirming the panel shows the correct human-readable label.

notes: Reviewed the integrated diff directly: migration.sql (additive, nullable, non-destructive), schema.prisma enum/field, users.ts's POST /users/:id/report interaction-path derivation and persistence, admin.ts's GET /admin/reports serialization, and the frontend rendering block. No authorization changes were made (admin router still gates ADMIN|MODERATOR at the router level; no route added; new field is set once at creation server-side from DB-verified interaction checks, never client-writable, never mutated by PATCH). No new data exposure -- the field reveals only a summary of the reporter/target relationship a moderator already sees via reportedUser/listing/reporterHistory on the same payload. No rate-limiting change needed since no new endpoint was added. The one real issue found is functional (contract mismatch between the two independently-implemented worktrees), not a security vulnerability per se, but it means the shipped evidence feature moderators are meant to rely on will display no information, undermining the explainability/audit-trail goal this task exists for -- routing back for a fix before this is considered done.
